title: Synthetic traffic harness and region-aware SLO-tuning dashboards for circuit-breaker/load-shed validation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build a reusable synthetic-traffic harness and a set of Grafana dashboards that let SRE/PE teams run controlled experiments to tune token-level latency SLIs, region failover policies, and circuit-breaker thresholds. The harness should be able to emulate token-by-token latency distributions, cold/warm KV cache states, bursty QPS patterns, and upstream error modes so that we can measure SLO burn and validate fallback behavior without impacting production traffic.

Why: We currently lack a safe, repeatable way to stress different parts of the stack and observe how our golden signals (latency, error rate, throughput, saturation) propagate across regions and trigger the adaptive load-shedding / circuit-breaker logic. This leads to ad-hoc tuning and surprise incidents during real-world region degradation.

Deliverables:
- A lightweight synthetic traffic generator (Go service) that can: emit requests with configurable token-length distributions, inject per-token latency jitter, toggle KV cache warm/cold, and simulate model-variant fallback sequences. Config in repo: infra/slo/synthetic.yaml.
- A set of Grafana dashboard panels grouped under "SLO Tuning - Synthetic Runs" that correlate: token-level p50/p95/p99 latencies, token loss/error rates, CPU/GPU queue lengths, KV cache hit ratio, per-region circuit-breaker state, and fallback invocation counts.
- A test harness to run scenario suites (e.g., regional outage, KV cache cold-start, model slow-down) with automatic report generation showing SLO burn, error-budget slope, and recommended threshold deltas.
- A standard runbook entry and a PR template to record experiment parameters, results, and the final threshold/rollout recommendation.

Success criteria:
- Engineers can run a scenario and get legible SLO burn reports within 10 minutes.
- Dashboard shows region-separated golden signals and highlights the earliest metric that predicts SLO breach.
- A/B experiment of two load-shed policies is reproducible and stores results in S3 for audit.

Notes on scope: This ticket focuses on instrumentation and dashboards plus the harness. Implementation of automatic tuning or policy rollout automation is out of scope and will be tracked separately.

Agreed to keep first-pass config surface minimal: token-length distribution, p(drop|error), per-token latency mean/stddev, KV cache hit ratio.

2026-02-20 - Aarav Patel: PoC generator checked in (infra/slo/synthetic-poc). Demonstrated single-region p99 spike injection. Next: add multi-region emitter and a mode to bias requests toward specific model variants so we can test fallback chains.

2026-02-27 - Design Review (Maya/Aarav/Leah): Dashboard wireframes reviewed. Decided panels must include: region split by control plane routing decision, request origin, token-count heatmap, and CB state timeline. Leah suggested a compact table showing recommended threshold changes based on observed SLO burn slope.

2026-03-03 - QoS Meeting: Ran initial 'KV cold-start' scenario; observed rapid p95 burn in region-us-west. Found telemetry gap: we don't tag token-latency spans with cache_warm boolean — filed follow-up ENG-48902 to add tag at runtime.
Action: for now annotate synthetic runs with synthetic.cache_warm=true so dashboards can filter.

2026-03-08 - Security Review (notes): Synthetic service will use a service token with limited scope to write to telemetry only. Confirmed no customer data will be used; runs use sanitized prompts. Audit trail will be kept in S3. Security sign-off pending minimal IAM review.

2026-03-10 - Aarav Patel: Implemented Grafana panels in dashboard folder grafana/dashboards/slo_tuning_synthetic.json. Added CI job that uploads run artifacts to S3 and posts a summary comment to the PR. Next steps: extend scenarios, harden harness, and schedule a tuning workshop with platform customers.
